previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Ms. ___ was admitted with shortness of breath and bright red blood per rectum. She has a complex history including asthma, COPD, prior lung and throat cancer, and chronic steroid use. Her dyspnea was attributed to post-influenza bronchitis and exacerbation of chronic lung disease, with CT showing progression of ground-glass opacities. Bronchoscopy revealed atypical squamous cells and abundant yeast, but no active infection; mucus plugging was cleared. She was started on Bactrim for PCP prophylaxis and received IV immunoglobulin for low IgG, suggesting possible CVID. Hemorrhoidal bleeding was confirmed by anoscopy with stable hemoglobin. Lisinopril was briefly started for hypertension but discontinued due to acute kidney injury. She improved clinically, was weaned off supplemental oxygen, and discharged home with home health, new medications including Spiriva and fexofenadine, and plans for outpatient follow-up with labs, imaging, and specialist visits.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year-old lady with a complicated past medical 
history including tracheal, lung, breast cancer (in remission); 
asthma, HTN, afib (during ICU hospitalization last year) on 
amiodorone but not on anticoagulation, CKD, referred from ___ 
for dyspnea, cough and increaing bilateral lower extremity edema 
concerning for acute on chronic diastolic heart failure.  

ACTIVE ISSUES:
====================
# Acute on chronic HFpEF: Constellation of symptoms consistent 
with exacarbation of now HFpEF (EF 60% in ___. Unclear what 
the trigger for this episode, but truly is multifactorial with 
the differential including ischemia (seems unlikely given 
negative CEsx2), COPD exacerbation (esp given cough/change in 
sputum production), lack of rate control of afib, and dietary 
indiscretion. The patient admitted to not being compliant with 
her furosemide at home as well. Potential that atrial 
fibrillation with asymptomatic rvr could be a component to her 
acute on chronic diastolic heart failure exacerbation. TTE was 
performed and showed LVEF 40-45% with left ventricular systolic 
function is mildly depressed secondary to mild global 
hypokinesis and septal dyssynchrony. The patient was diuresed 
with lasix IV and then transitioned to torsemide 80 mg daily. 
Admission weight 81.3kg with discharge weight 78.7 kg. Her 
carvedilol was switched to metoprolol for concern for 
bronchospasm with non-selective beta blockade of carvediolol. 
She was also continued on amlodipine. 
 
# COPD Exacerbation: Long history of COPD. Current respiratory 
decompensation seems more cardiac, but difficult to completely 
rule out COPD exacerbation and given that she reports worsening 
sputum production and change in nature, she should be treated 
for COPD exacerbation as well. She was initially treated with 
cefpodoxine for 5 days (azithromycin was avoided given QTc 440). 
Her prednisone was increased to 60mg daily and she received 60 
mg IV Solumedrol Q6H for one day before transitioning back to 
prednisone 60 mg and was discharged on a taper. She completed a 
course of doxycycline as well. She was seen by pulmonary who 
recommended budesonide nebulizers.  Urine legionella was 
negative. Blood cultures were negative. She was continued on 
Bactrim for PCP ___. She was maintained on standing 
ipratropium/albuterol nebs, guaifensin. She continued to have 
worsening sputum production despite having been treated with 
cefpodoxime and repeat CXR AP/Lateral was unrevealing for 
pneumonia. 

# Acute on chronic CKD: Most likely secondary to total body 
volume overload with third-spacing, and subsequently decreased 
kidney perfusion. She has known baseline CKD stage III-IV, with 
recent baseline Cr 1.7-2.0. She is not far from her baseline 
now. She started Bactrim for PCP prophylaxis while on steroids 
in ___, and there may be some increase in creatinine from 
this medication as well. The patient's Cr trended to 1.7 by 
discharge.

# Atrial fibrillation: Paroxysmal since MICU admission last 
year. Not on anticoagulation, but maintained on amiodarone.  She 
was continued on amiodarone. Her carvedilol was switched to 
metoprolol given the non-selective beta blocker with her 
underlying lung disease causing worsening bronchospasm. After 
long discussions as she was initially reluctant to take coumadin 
for the dietary indiscretions as well as from a personal 
anecdote, it was determined to start coumadin given her CHADS2 
score of 2. Her plavix was discontinued and she was started on 
coumadin to be followed by HCA anti-coag with INR of 2.1 on 
discharge. 

# Leukocytosis: The patient developed leukocytosis after the 
increase in her prednisone from 20mg at home to 60mg in the 
setting of her COPD exacerbation as described above. Urine and 
Blood cultures were negative and the patient did not have any 
localizing signs of infection.
 
CHRONIC ISSUES:
======================== 
# Hypertension: She was continued on amlodipine and carvedilol 
was transitioned to metoprolol, as above.

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
========================
# Anti-coagulation: CHADS2 score of 2 with starting coumadin to 
be managed by HCA anti-coagulation. 
# Discharge weight 78.7 kg.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Congestive heart failure, shortness of breath.

TECHNIQUE:  PA and lateral views of the chest.

COMPARISON:  Chest CT ___ and chest radiograph ___.

FINDINGS:

Study is limited due to patient rotation.  Heart size is normal.  The aortic
knob is calcified.  There is no overt pulmonary edema, but crowding of
bronchovascular structures is noted.  Linear and ill-defined opacities within
the left upper and mid lung fields are re- demonstrated, better assessed on
the recent chest CT, and may reflect residual inflammation or infection.
Postsurgical changes of the right lung with evidence of volume loss with
tenting of the right hemidiaphragm and linear opacities in the right upper
lung field compatible with prior radiation fibrosis are re- demonstrated.  No
focal consolidation, pleural effusion or pneumothorax is present.  Bilateral
shoulder arthroplasties are visualized.

IMPRESSION:

Limited exam.  Postsurgical and post treatment changes in the right lung,
similar compared to the prior exam.  Linear and ill-defined in opacities in
the left upper and mid lung fields are re- demonstrated, likely the residua of
prior infection or inflammation.

AP AND LATERAL CHEST OF ___.

COMPARISON:  ___ radiograph.

FINDINGS:  Marked volume loss in the right lung is related to previous right
upper lobe resection and radiation therapy as demonstrated on prior CT chest
of ___.  Cardiac silhouette is upper limits of normal in size. 
Pulmonary vascularity is within normal limits allowing for relatively low lung
volumes.  No focal areas of consolidation are present within the lungs, and
there are no definite pleural effusions.  Scarring along the right
hemidiaphragm contour appears unchanged as well as right apical thickening,
likely related to previous lung cancer treatment.

IMPRESSION:  No radiographic evidence of pneumonia.
